testName: Air Brakes Test #1 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: What type of force must emergency brakes use?
questions.explanation: Emergency brakes in an air brake system must use mechanical force. Air pressure can leak away, so mechanical force holds the brakes on.

questions.question: Which of these is NOT part of an air brake system?
questions.explanation: Air brake systems have three parts: the service brake system, the parking brake system, and the emergency brake system.

questions.question: If the low pressure warning light comes on while driving, what should you do?

options.text: Braking will only work if there is enough air in the tanks.
You can brake 14 times before the air runs out.
Continue driving normally and check the brakes later.
Continue driving but turn on emergency flashers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Braking will only work if there is enough air in the tanks.
questions.explanation: When the low air pressure warning light comes on, stop and park your vehicle as soon as possible. Your brakes will only work as long as air remains in the tanks.

questions.question: In an emergency stop, you should:

options.text: Lock the wheels and skid to a stop.
Keep your vehicle in a straight line.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your vehicle in a straight line.
questions.explanation: In an emergency stop, brake in a way that keeps your vehicle straight. You may use controlled braking or stab braking, but always keep the vehicle going straight while still being able to turn if needed.

questions.question: Emergency brakes:
questions.explanation: All trucks, truck tractors, and buses must have emergency brakes and parking brakes. These brakes must be held by mechanical force.

questions.question: Truck tractors with air brakes built on or after March 1, 1997 must have:
questions.explanation: All truck tractors with air brakes made on or after March 1, 1997 must have an Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS).

questions.question: Most heavy-duty vehicles use:
questions.explanation: Most heavy-duty vehicles use dual air brake systems. These have two separate braking systems that work with one set of controls. Each system controls brakes on different axles.

questions.question: If the spring brakes are on, you should:

options.text: Be extra careful because the brakes may fail.

questions.explanation: Do not use the brake pedal if the spring brakes are on. Using air pressure and spring force at the same time can damage the brakes.

questions.question: If your tractor has ABS but your trailer does not, the ABS:

options.text: Will still improve your steering control.
Will help others see when you brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Will still improve your steering control.
questions.explanation: If your tractor has ABS but your trailer does not, the ABS will still help you steer better. Watch the trailer and ease off the brakes if it starts to swing out.

questions.question: The ____ shows how much air pressure is in the tanks.
questions.explanation: Vehicles with air brakes must have a supply pressure gauge. This gauge tells the driver how much air pressure is in each air tank.

questions.question: During a walk-around inspection, check that brake drums have no cracks larger than ____ of the friction area width.
questions.explanation: Check the brake drums before you start driving. Do not drive if any brake drum has a crack larger than one half of the friction area width.

questions.question: What type of brakes do most heavy-duty vehicles have?
questions.explanation: Most heavy-duty vehicles have dual air brake systems for safety.

questions.question: If your vehicle has a front brake limiting valve, where should you set the control?

options.text: Set the control to the off position.
Keep the control at the halfway mark.

questions.explanation: Some older vehicles have a front brake limiting valve with "normal" and "slippery" settings. Leave it in the "normal" position to ensure normal stopping power.

questions.question: How do you stop a vehicle with air brakes?
questions.explanation: To stop an air brake vehicle, push the brake pedal down. The harder you press, the more air pressure is released.

questions.question: What happens if you press and release the brake pedal unnecessarily in an air brake system?

options.text: Release air faster than it can be replaced.
Add more air to the braking system.
Make the brake pedal more sensitive.

questions.correctAnswerText: Release air faster than it can be replaced.
questions.explanation: Unnecessary braking releases air from the system faster than the compressor can replace it.

questions.question: During a static leakage test, what is the maximum air leak rate allowed for a single vehicle with air brakes in one minute?
questions.explanation: During a static leakage test, a single air brake vehicle should lose no more than 2 psi in one minute. If it leaks faster, do not drive it.

questions.question: During an applied leakage test, what is the maximum air leak rate allowed for a single vehicle with air brakes?
questions.explanation: During an applied leakage test, a single air brake vehicle should lose no more than 3 psi in one minute.

questions.question: What equipment must truck tractors with air brakes built after March 1, 1997 have?
questions.explanation: Truck tractors with air brakes built on or after March 1, 1997 must have Anti-Lock Braking Systems (ABS).

questions.question: How often should you drain air tanks with manual drains?
questions.explanation: Drain air tanks at the end of each driving day to prevent oil and water buildup.

questions.question: When should a low air pressure warning signal turn on?

options.text: When tank pressure falls below 120 psi.
When tank pressure falls below 55 psi.
When tank pressure falls below 10 psi.
When tank pressure falls below 5 psi.

questions.correctAnswerText: When tank pressure falls below 55 psi.
questions.explanation: The low air pressure warning signal must turn on when tank pressure drops below 55 psi. The signal may be a light, buzzer, or wig wag.

questions.question: What do anti-lock brakes do?

options.text: Stop the wheels from locking up when braking hard
Stop a vehicle from speeding up while going uphill
Stop a vehicle from speeding up while going downhill

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop the wheels from locking up when braking hard
questions.explanation: Anti-lock brakes prevent the wheels from locking up when you brake hard.

questions.question: What is the most common type of foundation brake?
questions.explanation: The S-cam drum brake is the most common type of foundation brake.

questions.question: What happens if air pressure in the tanks drops below 60 psi?

options.text: A warning light will turn on
The vehicle will not shift out of gear

questions.correctAnswerText: A warning light will turn on
questions.explanation: When air pressure drops below 60 psi, a warning light or signal will activate to alert the driver.

questions.question: Most heavy-duty vehicles use ____ air brake systems.
questions.explanation: Most heavy-duty vehicles have dual air brake systems.

questions.question: When do spring brakes come on?

options.text: When air pressure drops too low
When a dashboard control is turned on
When tires have little tread left

questions.correctAnswerText: When air pressure drops too low
questions.explanation: Spring brakes turn on automatically when air pressure drops to an unsafe level. When you see a low pressure warning, safely pull off the road and stop the vehicle while you still have brake control.
